## A typical dose progression.

Providers may hold, change or stop a step based on your history, response and tolerability.

| Period | Reference dose | Phase |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–2 | 0.25 mg, then 0.5 mg | Starting and titration |
| Months 3–4 | 1 mg, then 1.7 mg | Titration |
| Month 5 onward | 1.7 mg or 2.4 mg | Maintenance range |

Reference dose progression for Semaglutide

This table summarizes the titration pattern for the corresponding FDA-approved formulation. It is not a prescription or instructions for self-adjustment. Compounded concentrations and prescribed schedules can differ. Use only the dose and measuring instructions on your pharmacy label, and ask your provider before any change.

The 6-month and annual plans do not renew automatically: continuing after the term needs a provider check-in, and no new term is charged without it. Prices are ongoing plan rates before any promotional discount.

EligibilityA licensed provider reviews your medical assessment and decides individually whether treatment is appropriate. Care is provided through Arora Health's provider network in all 50 states, not Puerto Rico.

ShippingIncluded in every plan. If prescribed, medication ships free overnight once compounded.

UNDERSTANDING YOUR OPTIONS

## A conversation.  _A personal decision._

Semaglutide acts on GLP-1 receptors involved in appetite regulation and slows stomach emptying. Your provider considers your medical needs, history and treatment goals before making a recommendation.

[Meet your care team](https://trytrimi.com/providers)

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

## Good questions.  _Clear answers._

A little clarity goes a long way.

[Ask our care team](https://trytrimi.com/contact)

Who can apply?

US residents aged 18 or older can complete the assessment. A provider licensed in your state reviews your health history and decides whether treatment is appropriate. Applying does not guarantee a prescription.

What does my plan include?

Medication, injection supplies, provider access and shipping are included. There are no separate enrollment, consultation, membership or shipping fees. Your plan price stays the same across prescribed doses.

When am I charged?

Payment is collected at checkout before provider review. If the provider decides treatment is not appropriate, your order is refunded in full under the refund policy. [Read the billing and refund terms.](https://trytrimi.com/refund-policy)

How do the billing plans work?

Choose monthly, quarterly, 6-month or annual billing. Multi-month rates are monthly equivalents, with the plan total billed upfront. The annual plan is a 12-month commitment. Review the full charge and renewal terms before checkout. [Read the billing and refund terms.](https://trytrimi.com/refund-policy)

Can I cancel or request a refund?

Monthly and 3-month plans renew automatically unless you turn renewal off, which does not end a term you have already paid for. 6-month and annual plans do not renew automatically. Refunds follow the published refund policy, including its conditional 6-month money-back policy. Contact the care team to review your situation. [Read the billing and refund terms.](https://trytrimi.com/refund-policy)

When will my medication arrive?

Provider review typically takes 12-24 hours. If prescribed, your medication ships free overnight once compounded. The full process from signup to delivery typically takes 2-4 days; timing can vary.

Do I need insurance?

No. Trimi does not bill insurance. HSA/FSA payment is accepted, but your plan administrator determines expense eligibility. Do not assume that your insurance will reimburse a purchase.

Is compounded semaglutide FDA-approved?

Compounded medications are not FDA-approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before marketing. They should be considered only when an approved drug cannot meet a patient's medical needs; your provider must evaluate your individual case.

How is my dose chosen?

Your provider chooses the dose and schedule based on your history and response. Follow your prescription and the pharmacy's measuring instructions. Compounded concentrations can vary, so never copy another person's syringe units or adjust your dose yourself.

## Your safety comes first.

[Read full safety information](https://trytrimi.com/important-safety-information)

### Compounding & side effects

Compounded medications are not FDA-approved. FDA does not review them for safety, effectiveness or quality.

Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation and abdominal discomfort can occur. Tell your provider about symptoms that persist or interfere with eating or drinking.

### Important risks

Serious risks include pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, dehydration-related kidney injury and severe allergic reactions. Approved semaglutide labeling carries a thyroid C-cell tumor warning based on animal studies; human risk is unknown. Do not use with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.

### Talk with your provider

Share all medicines, medical conditions and pregnancy or breastfeeding plans with your provider. Insulin and some diabetes medicines can increase low-blood-sugar risk. Seek urgent care for severe abdominal pain or trouble breathing. This summary does not replace your prescription or the full safety information.

About published semaglutide research

**STEP 1:** 14.9% average weight reduction at 68 weeks. Average weight reduction in adults without diabetes receiving semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly plus lifestyle support. The placebo group lost 2.4% on average.

This trial studied the formulation used for an FDA-approved medicine. It did not test Trimi's compounded preparation or establish its safety or effectiveness. Compounded medications are not FDA-approved. Individual results vary.

[Wilding et al., New England Journal of Medicine, 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33567185/)
